prompt.context_jp: 冬の夕暮れ、新宿の街角には冷たい風___吹き抜けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 冬の夕暮れ、新宿の街角には冷たい風___吹き抜けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that fits this scene-setting description.

feedback.correct_en: This sentence opens the chapter and introduces 'cold wind' as new information in the scene. New information in a descriptive opener takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'cold wind' a known topic, which doesn't fit a first-line scene description. を doesn't work because 吹き抜ける is intransitive here.

contrast_examples.en: A wind is blowing. (observed, new info)
The wind is cold. (wind as known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 名残を惜しむ気持ちを隠しきれず、女___なかなか男の袖を放そうとしなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 女___なかなか男の袖を放そうとしなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the already-introduced 'woman'.

feedback.correct_en: The woman has already been introduced earlier in the scene; here she is the topic whose behavior is being described, so は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as new information, which clashes with the fact that we've been following her. に marks a goal/recipient, not fitting here.

prompt.context_jp: 寄り添う二人の姿を、少し離れた物陰からじっと見つめる人影___あった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...じっと見つめる人影___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces this previously-unseen figure.

feedback.correct_en: The 'figure' is first introduced here as new information in an 〜がある existential pattern — classic が for new referent.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose we already know this figure. も would mean 'also,' but nothing prior sets up that contrast.

contrast_examples.en: There was a man there. (newly introduced)

prompt.context_jp: 張り詰めた空気の中、最初に口を開いたの___布施だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 最初に口を開いたの___布施だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this cleft identifying sentence.

feedback.correct_en: In the cleft pattern 〜のは Xだった, は marks the presupposed description and X is the identified answer. は is required here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot follow の in this cleft frame. The description 'the one who spoke first' is the topic, and 布施 is the new identification.

contrast_examples.en: The one who came is Tanaka.

prompt.context_jp: 「こういうのって普通 床嶋君がやるんじゃないの？」「私___デスクで ナースじゃありません｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___デスクで、ナースじゃありません。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Tokoshima uses to contrast herself with a nurse.

feedback.correct_en: She's drawing a contrast: 'As for me, I'm a desk worker, not a nurse.' Contrastive/topical は fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like she's suddenly identifying who the desk worker is, missing the contrastive 'I, unlike what you expect' nuance.

contrast_examples.en: I'm a desk worker (as for me).
I'm the desk worker (identifying the one).

prompt.context_jp: 「まさか ...ブロンズ住もう君___人を傷つけるとはね｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: ブロンズ住もう君___人を傷つけるとはね。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this 〜とは exclamation.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the surprised 〜とはね clause, 住もう君 is the subject of an unexpected event. Subjects in such embedded 'who-would-have-thought' clauses take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would promote the statue to topic of the whole surprise, which doesn't match this one-event exclamation. を would require a transitive object relation, but the role here is subject.

contrast_examples.jp: まさか彼が来るとはね。
contrast_examples.en: Who'd have thought HE would come.

prompt.context_jp: 結局その日、契約書に___一つの署名もされなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 契約書に___一つの署名もされなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that emphasizes 'not even one signature.'

feedback.correct_en: には here sets up a contrastive 'as for the contract, not even one signature' frame, highlighting the complete lack of signatures.
feedback.incorrect_en: にが is ungrammatical in this location pattern. にで doesn't form a natural particle string here.

prompt.context_jp: 差し込む朝の光の中に、すらりとした長身の男___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...すらりとした長身の男___立っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for this newly-seen figure in the doorway.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is pointing out, for the first time, a man standing in the light — classic 'presentational' が introducing a new figure to the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply we already knew this man and are now predicating about him. も would need a prior comparable figure, which there isn't.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアの前に男が立っていた。
contrast_examples.en: A man was standing in front of the door.

contrast_examples.jp: その男は留守堂だった。

prompt.context_jp: 坂の頂上に、一人の女性___姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_jp: 坂の頂上に、一人の女性___姿を現した。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces 'one woman' appearing at the top of the hill.

feedback.correct_en: The quantified indefinite 一人の女性 is new to the scene, and 姿を現す announces an appearance — that's exactly when が is used.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't attach to an indefinite like 一人の女性 as a topic here. を would conflict with the already-present 姿を.

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の男が入ってきた。

prompt.context_jp: 小さな契約の一件一件が営業所の数字を支えていることを、彼___誰よりもよく知っている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼___誰よりもよく知っている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Yashiro, whose knowledge is being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: Yashiro is the established topic of the paragraph, and the sentence makes a general characterization about him. Topical/characterizing は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like 'HE (of all people) is the one who knows,' which is a different, exhaustive-listing nuance that doesn't match the quiet narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼が一番よく知っている。
contrast_examples.en: HE's the one who knows best. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 激高した相手を前に、万智___あえて火に油を注ぐような一言を放ったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 万智___あえて火に油を注ぐような一言を放ったのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Machi in this explanatory 〜のだ sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Machi is the already-known main character; the sentence explains what she did (〜のだ). Topical は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce Machi as if newly discovered, which is odd when the whole chapter revolves around her.

contrast_examples.jp: 万智は何も言わなかった。

prompt.context_jp: 二人が肩___並べて歩き出すと、街のざわめきがその後ろ姿を包み込んだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 二人が肩___並べて歩き出すと…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside the set phrase 'walk shoulder to shoulder.'

feedback.correct_en: 肩を並べる ('line up shoulders' → walk side by side) is a fixed collocation where 肩 is the direct object of 並べる, so を is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 'shoulders' the subject of 並べる (transitive), which breaks the structure. に would mean 'to the shoulder,' nonsensical here.

prompt.context_jp: 屋代は万智を部屋の隅___呼び、声を落とした。
prompt.prompt_jp: 屋代は万智を部屋の隅___呼び…
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the destination of 'calling (someone) over.'

feedback.correct_en: 呼ぶ in the sense of 'call (someone) over to a place' takes に for the destination.
feedback.incorrect_en: で would mark the location of an action (he called her AT the corner), but the point is she's being moved TO the corner. を is already taken by 万智.

prompt.context_jp: ママのこころは、ただならぬ様子の客___、いつもより控えめな笑顔を向けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...ただならぬ様子の客___...笑顔を向けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking who the smile is directed toward.

feedback.correct_en: 〜を向ける ('direct X toward Y') marks Y with に. The smile goes toward the customer.
feedback.incorrect_en: を is already taken by 笑顔. で would mark means or location, neither of which fits a target of direction.

prompt.context_jp: 男の鞄からのぞく封筒には、見覚えのある不動産会社の名前___印刷されていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...不動産会社の名前___印刷されていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'the real-estate company's name' noticed on the envelope.

feedback.correct_en: The name is being noticed/discovered on the envelope — a textbook 'perception of new information' use of が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make the company name a known topic, which contradicts the moment of discovery. を doesn't fit the intransitive 印刷されていた (passive state).

contrast_examples.jp: 封筒に名前が書いてあった。
contrast_examples.en: There was a name written on the envelope.

contrast_examples.jp: 名前はもう消えている。

prompt.context_jp: 「生涯 まり以外___心を奪われることはないよ｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 生涯 まり以外___心を奪われることはないよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle after 'anyone other than Mari.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜に心を奪われる ('to have one's heart stolen by ~') takes に for the agent/stimulus. 'By anyone other than Mari' → まり以外に.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would require a different verb structure. を is already attached to 心.

prompt.context_jp: 湊人の言葉のあと、応接スペースには重い沈黙___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 応接スペースには重い沈黙___落ちた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the 'heavy silence' that falls.

feedback.correct_en: The silence is a new event emerging in the scene (沈黙が落ちる). Emergence/occurrence calls for が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 'the silence' as a known topic, but it's just now arising. を doesn't fit this intransitive event.

contrast_examples.en: The silence was long. (describing known silence)

prompt.context_jp: 「今日 契約するはずだった 家のことですが いったん ___ 戻して いただきたいんですが｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: いったん ___ 戻していただきたいんですが。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression that means 'put it on hold / back to a clean slate.'

feedback.correct_en: 白紙に戻す is the set business phrase for 'scrap it and start over / revert to a clean sheet.' That's exactly what Minato is asking for here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 空白に戻す isn't a fixed phrase. ゼロに戻す exists but means 'reset to zero' (numbers/counters), not 'cancel a planned agreement.'

contrast_examples.en: Scrap the plan / go back to square one.

contrast_examples.jp: カウントをゼロに戻す。

prompt.context_jp: 激高した相手を前に、万智はあえて ___ ような一言を放ったのだ。
prompt.prompt_jp: あえて ___ ような一言を放ったのだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the idiom meaning 'add fuel to the fire.'

feedback.correct_en: 火に油を注ぐ literally 'pour oil on the fire' = provoke an already-angry situation. Machi deliberately inflamed the furious husband.
feedback.incorrect_en: 水を差す means 'throw cold water on / dampen,' the opposite effect. 泥を塗る means 'bring disgrace upon,' which is about reputation, not provoking anger.

contrast_examples.jp: 怒ってる人に油を注ぐな。
contrast_examples.en: Don't add fuel to an angry person's fire.

contrast_examples.jp: 盛り上がりに水を差す。

prompt.context_jp: 「今夜は実家に帰しました｡ そこで きっと ___ 冷やしてくれると思います｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: きっと ___ 冷やしてくれると思います。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes 'cool one's head / calm down.'

feedback.correct_en: 頭を冷やす is the fixed idiom for 'cool down / think things over calmly.' Oda hopes Mari will regain her composure.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心を冷やす isn't an idiom in this sense. 顔を冷やす would literally mean cooling your face, not calming emotions.

contrast_examples.jp: 少し頭を冷やしてこい。
contrast_examples.en: Go cool your head for a bit.

prompt.context_jp: その光景を、物陰から万智たちが ___ のんで見守っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 物陰から万智たちが ___ のんで見守っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes 'with bated breath.'

feedback.correct_en: 固唾をのむ is the set phrase meaning 'watch tensely / hold one's breath in suspense' — perfect for this stakeout scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息をのむ exists but means 'gasp in amazement' at a sudden sight, not sustained tense watching. 言葉をのむ means 'swallow one's words,' a different situation.

contrast_examples.jp: 試合を固唾をのんで見守る。
contrast_examples.en: Watch the match with bated breath.

prompt.context_jp: 今月の売上見込みが大幅に減少するのではないかと、皆が内心で ___ でいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 皆が内心で ___ でいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the phrase meaning 'to be anxious / fret inwardly.'

feedback.correct_en: 気をもむ means 'to worry / fret' about an outcome one can't control — exactly what the staff are doing about this month's sales.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気をつける means 'be careful,' not anxious worrying. 気を引く means 'draw someone's attention/interest.'

contrast_examples.jp: 結果が心配で気をもむ。

prompt.context_jp: 塵も積もれば ___ となるように、小さな偶然も重なれば、やがて運命へと変わるのである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も積もれば ___ となる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that completes this proverb.

feedback.correct_en: The proverb is 塵も積もれば山となる ('even dust piled up becomes a mountain') — small things add up.
feedback.incorrect_en: 海 (sea) and 林 (forest) are not the imagery used in this fixed proverb.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

prompt.context_jp: 「他人の目なぞ ___ ！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 他人の目なぞ ___ ！
prompt.prompt_en: Choose Machi's catch-phrase meaning 'a trivial matter / piece of cake.'

feedback.correct_en: 屁の河童 ('a kappa of a fart') is Machi's signature idiom meaning 'nothing to worry about / no big deal.' It fits her dismissive attitude toward 'other people's eyes.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 猫の額 means 'tiny space' (cat's forehead). 馬の耳 (horse's ear) belongs to 馬の耳に念仏 — advice falling on deaf ears.

contrast_examples.en: That's a piece of cake / no big deal.
A garden the size of a cat's forehead.

prompt.context_jp: 「一回 ___ なければ ダメだと思ったのです｡」
prompt.prompt_jp: 一回 ___ なければ ダメだと思ったのです。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'make (his pent-up anger) explode / let it all out.'

feedback.correct_en: 爆発させる ('cause to explode') is the standard metaphor for letting emotions burst out. Machi needed Oda to vent his rage first.
feedback.incorrect_en: 炎上させる is used mostly for fires or online flame-wars, not personal emotion. 噴火させる (cause to erupt) is used only for volcanoes, not people's feelings.

prompt.context_jp: Scene-setting opening line.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as a novel's opening scene description?

choices.text: 冬の夕暮れ、新宿の街角には冷たい風が吹き抜けていた。
冷たい風は冬の夕暮れ、新宿の街角で吹き抜けていた。

feedback.correct_en: Opening scene lines in Japanese narrative typically front the setting (time, place) and introduce the new element (風) with が. The actual text does exactly this.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B topicalizes 冷たい風 with は, which presupposes the wind is already known — awkward for a very first line.

contrast_examples.jp: 公園には子供が遊んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: Children were playing in the park. (natural scene opening)

contrast_examples.jp: 子供は公園で遊んでいた。
contrast_examples.en: The (specific) children were playing in the park.

prompt.context_jp: Machi's confident declaration to Yashiro about selling the Yasoda house.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more like Machi's signature confident style?

choices.text: 私に売れない家はありません！
私は売れない家がありません！

feedback.correct_en: The template 〜に…はない emphasizes that for ME specifically, no unsellable house exists. It's a punchy, idiomatic boast and matches the show's actual line.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B is grammatically awkward — 'I don't have houses that can't be sold' confuses possession and generalization, losing the declarative punch.

contrast_examples.jp: 私にできないことはない。
私はできないことがない。
contrast_examples.en: (awkward) I don't have things I can't do.

prompt.context_jp: Introducing a watching figure for the first time.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is more natural for introducing a brand-new figure to the scene?

choices.text: 寄り添う二人の姿を、少し離れた物陰からじっと見つめる人影があった。
寄り添う二人の姿を、少し離れた物陰からじっと見つめる人影はあった。

feedback.correct_en: The 〜があった existential introduces a new, previously-unseen figure — standard narrative device.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜はあった sounds like a contrastive 'well, at least there WAS a figure,' implying a comparison with something expected absent. Odd on first mention.

contrast_examples.jp: 手紙はあったが、短かった。
contrast_examples.en: There was a letter (sure), but it was short.

prompt.context_jp: Machi apologizing to the client for Niwano's blurting things out.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version matches Machi's business-polite register to the client?

choices.text: 庭野が余計なことを申しまして お許しくださいませ。
庭野が余計なこと言っちゃって ごめんね。

feedback.correct_en: To a client, Machi uses humble 申しまして and the polite request くださいませ — appropriate business keigo.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B is casual peer-level speech (言っちゃって / ごめんね) — totally inappropriate when addressing a customer whose deal just collapsed.

contrast_examples.jp: ご迷惑をおかけして申し訳ございません。
contrast_examples.en: We deeply apologize for the trouble. (to a client)
Sorry for the trouble. (to a friend)

prompt.context_jp: Identifying who first broke the tense silence.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version naturally expresses 'the one who spoke first was Fuse'?

choices.text: 張り詰めた空気の中、最初に口を開いたのは布施だった。
張り詰めた空気の中、最初に口を開いたのが布施はだった。

feedback.correct_en: The cleft frame 〜のは Xだ identifies X as the answer. The actual sentence uses this pattern cleanly.
feedback.incorrect_en: Version B scrambles particles — のが with 布施は is ungrammatical. You can't double-mark the predicate noun with は in a copula.

contrast_examples.jp: 答えたのは山田だった。
contrast_examples.en: The one who answered was Yamada.
